neighbours.label: the comma ending the conditional part of a math word problem with a fraction or percent (If 3/5 of a group were girls,)
fire: If 2/3 of a class were boys, and there were 18 pupils, how many?
If 1/4 of the apples were red, and there were 40 apples, how many?
If 3/8 of a pizza was eaten, and there were 8 slices, how many?
If 40 percent of the team were girls, and there were 15 players, how many?
If 1/5 of a farm is corn, and there are 50 acres, how many?
If 3/4 of the seats were taken, and there were 60 seats, how many?
If 2/5 of the books are new, and there are 30 books, how many?
If 25 percent of the eggs broke, and there were 12 eggs, how many?
quiet: Most of a class were boys, and there were 18 pupils in the room today.
Many of the apples were red, and there were 40 apples in the basket.
Part of a pizza was eaten, and there were 8 slices on the table.
Most of the team were girls, and there were 15 players on the bus.
Part of a farm is corn, and there are 50 acres in the valley.
Most of the seats were taken, and there were 60 seats in the hall.
Some of the books are new, and there are 30 books on the shelf.
Many of the eggs broke, and there were 12 eggs in the carton.

short: ',' after a fraction in a word problem
notes: Card: ' percent' x4, ',' x2, '.' x2, '\n' x2, ' hour' x2, ' cent'. Probes: ',' after 'If 3/5 of a group were girls' 0.580, ' percent' 0.249, ' cent' 0.147, 'Tell him' 0.134. A guess from the top peak; the percent words are not claimed.
